sections.h2: Where is Marion County, West Virginia, and how does property tax work there?
sections.html:
Marion County is in north-central West Virginia along the Monongahela River, with Fairmont as the county seat. The Virginia Assembly created it on January 14, 1842, from parts of Monongalia and Harrison counties, and it was named for General Francis Marion. It covers 312 square miles and borders Monongalia, Taylor, Harrison and Wetzel counties.

Fairmont, Mannington and Pleasant Valley are the cities, and the towns include Fairview, Barrackville, Farmington, Grant Town, Monongah, Rivesville, Whitehall and Worthington. Interstate 79 crosses the county, with U.S. 19 and U.S. 250. Your tax category depends on whether the house sits in a town or in open country, since property inside a municipality is taxed in a different class from property outside it.

sections.h2: What shaped Marion County's housing stock and economy?
sections.html:
Coal and the railroad built Marion County, and the age of its houses still shows it. The Baltimore and Ohio Railroad reached the area in June 1852, which helped open the coal fields. On December 6, 1907, an explosion at the Fairmont Coal Company's Nos. 6 and 8 mines in Monongah killed 362 miners, and it has been described as the worst mining disaster in American history.

The Census figures shown on this page put the median Marion County home at a build year of 1960. Houses of that age often need roofs, wiring or foundation work before a mortgage lender will accept them. Sellers who cannot or do not want to spend that money often look at selling as-is.

The county's own tax calendar and property record cards give a useful starting point. Property record cards dating from 2001 can be searched online, which helps a seller see how the assessor describes square footage and condition before the February review.

sections.h2: What is the Marion County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The Marion County Sheriff publishes a full calendar, and it adds dates beyond the basic state schedule. The sheriff mails statements and starts collecting on July 15, with a 2.5 percent discount if the first half is paid by September 1. After that, interest of 9 percent a year, or 0.75 percent a month, applies to unpaid first-half tax from October 2.

Notice that once April 2 passes, the calendar says only a full-year payment may be accepted. A seller who lets the spring installment slip can end up needing more cash at closing than expected.

sections.h2: How do you reach the Marion County Sheriff's Tax Office?
sections.html:
The Sheriff acts as tax collector and treasurer from the first floor of the J. Harper Meredith Building, 200 Jackson Street, Room 101, Fairmont, WV 26554. Mail goes to PO Box 1348, Fairmont, WV 26555-1348. The phone is 304-367-5310, and the posted hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • Online tax inquiry and payments are listed at wvpropertytaxes.com, with a Software Systems portal for the Marion County search.
  • Personal property assessment questions can go to the assessor at 367-5413.
  • The Sheriff's office notifies registered owners and lienholders by certified mail around September 1 when property is headed toward the lien process.

sections.h2: Who sells delinquent real estate tax liens in Marion County now?
sections.html:
The West Virginia State Auditor, since the Legislature passed Senate Bill 552. The Marion County Sheriff's notice says county sheriffs no longer conduct the sale of delinquent real estate tax liens. On the close of business October 31 each year the Sheriff must certify the list of delinquent properties to the State Auditor's Office.

After that point, an owner has to contact the Auditor's Office to redeem the property, not the sheriff. The notice also points to Chapter 11A of the West Virginia Code for the full text. If your Marion County house shows unpaid tax, move before October 31. After certification the cost and the paperwork both go up, and the owner deals with a state office in Charleston rather than the courthouse in Fairmont.

A cash sale can happen before or after certification, but earlier is simpler. We buy houses as-is in Fairmont, Mannington, Monongah and the rest of Marion County, and the payoff is handled at closing.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Marion County valuation?
sections.html:
Protests go to the Marion County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which begins meeting February 1 and ends no later than the last day of February. West Virginia assesses at 60 percent of true and actual value, so the board checks that your number does not exceed that share of what the house is worth.

You can appeal the board's order to the Office of Tax Appeals by March 31, and the proof standard throughout is a preponderance of the evidence. Owners 65 and older, or permanently and totally disabled, may claim the $20,000 homestead exemption after meeting the state residency rule.

Bring the evidence with you. A written repair estimate, photos of a failing foundation or roof and two or three recent nearby sale prices carry more weight than a general complaint that the bill feels high.

sections.h2: What are the regular tax rate ceilings that apply in Marion County?
sections.html:
State law caps the regular levy for each kind of taxing body and each class of property, in cents per $100 of assessed value. The county sets the actual rate within those caps, and voters can add excess levies by referendum, which the Marion County levy figure above shows it uses.

County28.6057.2057.20
Schools45.9091.8091.80
Municipal25.00none50.00

Class II is owner-occupied residential. Class III is other property outside a municipality, and Class IV is other property inside one. The state lists totals of $1.00, $1.50 and $2.00 per $100 for Classes II, III and IV, so a rental or vacant house can cost about twice as much to carry as the same house occupied by its owner.

As an illustration, a $100,000 owner-occupied house in Fairmont is assessed at 60 percent, or $60,000, which is $600 a year at the regular ceiling, before excess levies. A neighbor's rental of the same value is taxed in Class IV at up to $1,200. Use these as rough checks, not quotes. If you own a Marion County rental and want out, call (424) 435-2326 for an as-is cash offer.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Marion County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Sheriff's Tax Office, 200 Jackson Street, Room 101, Fairmont, WV 26554, or mail to PO Box 1348, Fairmont, WV 26555-1348. Online payment is available through the county's tax portal.

faqs.q: What is the Marion County first-half discount deadline?
faqs.a: Pay by September 1 to earn the 2.5 percent discount. Interest of 9 percent a year starts on October 2 for unpaid first-half tax.

faqs.q: Who runs the delinquent tax lien sale in Marion County?
faqs.a: The State Auditor's Office does. The Sheriff certifies the delinquent list to the Auditor by October 31 each year, and owners redeem through the Auditor.

faqs.q: What is Marion County's phone number for taxes?
faqs.a: The Sheriff's Tax Office is at 304-367-5310, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marion County house with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the payoff from your proceeds at closing, and an earlier sale avoids the extra fees that are added as the calendar moves forward.
